description:
The proposal relates to internal alterations within a Grade II listed flat. 
GENERAL:I propose the installation of internal 42mm insulated plasterboard to the exterior wall to improve the energy efficiency of the property. 
I propose the installation of approximately 50mm insulation on the ceiling, fixed to timber battens. 
Existing decorative features, including cornices, will be retained and unaffected by the proposed works.
The proposal includes installation of a low-temperature wet (warm water) underfloor heating system throughout the flat, including the hallway and bathroom, following the removal of the existing carpet finishes. New hard floor finishes will be installed above. This system is considered more energy efficient than conventional radiator-based heating systems due to its ability to operate effectively at lower flow temperatures. 
Internal doors and skirtings to rooms and the bathroom will be replaced with period-style Art Deco doors and skirtings.
The entrance door to the flat is also proposed to be replaced on a like-for-like basis, replicating the existing design, including colour in order to maintain visual consistency of the building.

LAYOUT CHANGE: Relocation of the existing kitchen to an adjacent wall shared with the bathroom to improve functionality and use of space. It's designed to utilise existing service connections adjacent to the bathroom.
The existing dining area would form a bedroom space, benefiting from access to the existing window. I also propose the removal of two internal partition walls enclosing the existing kitchen area. These partitions are understood to be non-structural and this change would create a more open and functional arrangement.
I propose the relocation of the existing boiler to a cupboard within the hallway, in order to provide a more appropriate and practical arrangement within the flat and to improve residential amenity. This will involve the repositioning of the existing flue by approximately 1.5 metres. A new flue opening will be formed, designed to match the existing in terms of size and appearance, while the existing flue opening will be carefully closed and made good using matching materials to ensure it is not visually prominent. I prefer this relocation to avoid keeping the boiler in the sleeping areas, improving comfort and amenity.

Bathroom: replacement of the existing bathtub with a shower enclosure, installation of new wall and floor finishes. To address existing condensation issues, I propose the installation of thin-profile insulation (including approximately 6mm tile backer insulation board) to external walls within the bathroom. 
All works will be carried out by suitably qualified professionals and are designed to minimise impact on the historic fabric and character of the listed building. No changes are proposed to the external appearance of the building other than the minor alteration associated with the repositioned flue.
